final_proof:
Let the sequence of groups be
\[
G_1\xrightarrow{f_1}G_2\xrightarrow{f_2}G_3\xrightarrow{f_3}\cdots,
\]
where every \(f_n\) is a group homomorphism. For \(r\ge n\), write \(f_{r,n}:G_n\to G_r\) for the composite \(f_{r-1}\circ\cdots\circ f_n\), with \(f_{n,n}=\operatorname{id}_{G_n}\). Thus \(G_\infty\) consists of the equivalence classes \([x,n]\) of pairs \((x,n)\), where
\[
(x,n)\sim(y,m)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{there is some }r\ge n,m\text{ such that }f_{r,n}(x)=f_{r,m}(y).
\]
Let \(h_n:G_n\to H\) be the given compatible family of group homomorphisms, so \(h_{n+1}\circ f_n=h_n\) for every \(n\). The proposed map is \(h_\infty([x,n])=h_n(x)\).

By induction on \(r-n\), compatibility gives
\[
h_r\circ f_{r,n}=h_n \qquad (r\ge n).
\]
Suppose that \([x,n]=[y,m]\). By the definition of the equivalence relation, there is an \(r\ge n,m\) for which \(f_{r,n}(x)=f_{r,m}(y)\). Consequently,
\[
h_n(x)=h_r(f_{r,n}(x))=h_r(f_{r,m}(y))=h_m(y).
\]
Hence the prescribed value of \(h_\infty\) is independent of the representative, so \(h_\infty\) is well-defined.

Now take \([x,n],[y,m]\in G_\infty\), and choose \(r\ge n,m\). Multiplication in the direct limit is computed at a common stage, so
\[
[x,n][y,m]=[f_{r,n}(x)f_{r,m}(y),r].
\]
Using first that \(h_r\) is a homomorphism and then the compatibility identity above, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_\infty([x,n][y,m])
 &=h_r(f_{r,n}(x)f_{r,m}(y))\\
 &=h_r(f_{r,n}(x))h_r(f_{r,m}(y))\\
 &=h_n(x)h_m(y)\\
 &=h_\infty([x,n])h_\infty([y,m]).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(h_\infty\) preserves the group operation. In particular, it also sends the identity to the identity, either by this equality or directly from \(h_n(e_{G_n})=e_H\). Therefore \(h_\infty:G_\infty\to H\) is a well-defined group homomorphism.
